candidates.current_wording: Capitalism has produced broad prosperity across historical contexts.
candidates.why_fails: Civilizationally sweeping; no registered sources; unfalsifiable as written.
candidates.strongest_defensible: Market-oriented growth has been associated with large gains in material living standards in many countries and periods, with important exceptions and distributional conflicts.
candidates.proposed_replacement: In many countries and periods, market-oriented growth has been associated with large gains in material living standards, with important exceptions, crises, and distributional conflicts that must be scoped before public wording.
contrary_evidence: Cross-country and within-country experiences vary widely.
removed: Universal 'capitalism has produced', implied inevitability across all contexts
candidates.confidence: Very Low until sourced modules exist
candidates.governance_recommendation: REWRITE — then open historical modules before any Supports path.

candidates.current_wording: Broader ownership participation would shift many households from wage-only dependence toward multi-source capital ownership.
candidates.why_fails: Uses SCF/DFA concentration sources to support a redesign forecast.
candidates.fit_defect: NON-SUPPORTING / CAUSAL OVERREACH / FORECAST WITHOUT MODEL
candidates.strongest_defensible: U.S. household wealth is highly concentrated; effects of broader ownership participation on household income composition are untested predictions.
candidates.proposed_replacement: U.S. household wealth is highly concentrated; whether broader ownership participation would shift households toward multi-source capital income is an untested design prediction requiring modeling and pilots.
contrary_evidence: Concentration facts do not validate ownership-redesign outcomes.
candidates.confidence: High for concentration clause; Very Low for prediction clause
candidates.governance_recommendation: REWRITE (split descriptive vs predictive) — or SPLIT into two claims.

candidates.current_wording: Online commerce can extract spending from local economies via platform concentration and wealth leakage.
candidates.why_fails: Leakage/extraction unproven; scale sources do not establish the mechanism claim.
candidates.strongest_defensible: Online commerce is a material share of U.S. retail sales; local wealth effects require dedicated studies; pre-Wayfair tax myths are outdated.
candidates.proposed_replacement: Online commerce is a material share of U.S. retail sales; effects on local spending, platform margins, and community wealth require dedicated leakage/multiplier studies and must not recycle pre-Wayfair tax myths.
contrary_evidence: Consumer choice and hybrid local/online sellers; Wayfair collection authority.
candidates.confidence: High for retail share; Low for local effects until studies registered
candidates.governance_recommendation: REWRITE — then keep leakage as open research, not claim fact.

candidates.current_wording: Property taxation can threaten ownership security for some households.
candidates.why_fails: 'Threaten ownership security' overclaims relative to burden/relief evidence.
candidates.strongest_defensible: Property taxes can impose high burdens relative to income or liquidity for some households; they remain a central local revenue source.
candidates.proposed_replacement: Property taxes can impose high burdens relative to income or liquidity for some households, motivating targeted relief design; they are also a central, relatively stable local revenue source.
contrary_evidence: Lincoln Institute emphasizes property-tax strengths and targeted relief over blunt limits.

candidates.current_wording: Corporate relocation and rural structural decline can drain community capacity, including local banking and healthcare access.
candidates.why_fails: Bundles corporate relocation causality with documented rural structural stress.
candidates.strongest_defensible: Rural structural decline can erode community capacity in population, banking, and healthcare access; relocation is a plausible separate mechanism.
candidates.proposed_replacement: Rural structural decline can erode community capacity (population, banking, healthcare access); corporate relocation is a plausible contributing mechanism requiring separate causal modules.
contrary_evidence: Heterogeneous nonmetro outcomes; some post-2020 gains.
removed: Joint proven package of relocation + decline
candidates.governance_recommendation: REWRITE or SPLIT — optional fifth repair beyond original four.
